column1: # Retrieval eval set for etcd. See tests/eval/README.md for the format.
# repository: https://github.com/etcd-io/etcd
# revision: 1b5ba72405d62c16f3011a7bfb56a6a721ee51a3
# Targets are callables of 21-150 lines, each name-unique within its file.
# etcd puts an interface beside its implementation often enough that 12% of
# callable names repeat, and a target with a same-named sibling nearby tends to
# be unanswerable in practice.
# No target is generated protobuf, a _test.go file, or the framework code under
# tests/, which carries the ranker's 0.3x test-path penalty.
# Rows 1-15 and 16-30 were written separately and score differently (recall@5 20% and 7%).
# The gap tracks how strictly each author avoided reusing the domain words that
# appear in the answer, not retrieval quality: the half that leans on them hands
# the lexical retriever free hits. Judge a ranking change by the per-query diff,
# never by the summary line, and never by comparing this corpus's summary
# against another one's.
delete every key a lease was holding once that lease is given up
gather the leases whose deadline already passed so they can be dropped
catch up streams that fell behind by replaying stored events out of the backend
tell a caught-up stream the current revision when nothing has changed for it
drop superseded versions of a key below a revision, a batch at a time
rewrite the database file into a compacted copy to give free pages back
check whether the permissions a user was granted cover the whole span being touched
refuse a membership change that would leave the cluster without a quorum
close the current log segment, preallocate the next file and start writing there
ship a database snapshot over http to a follower that lagged past the log
ask every peer for the hash of its key space and alarm when they disagree
wait for the leader to confirm the index before serving a strongly consistent read
take a place in line for leadership and block until every earlier contender is gone
return every stored range that overlaps the one being asked about
reopen the broken grpc stream and resume from the last revision seen
back up the last log file and cut it back to the last complete record after a crash
walk every key in the database at boot to rebuild the in-memory index and reattach leases
record that a key is gone by writing a marker at the next revision and detaching its lease
serve a read by combining pending in-memory writes with what the on-disk bucket holds
sign a bearer token carrying the user name and auth revision after a successful login
give a role read or write access over a span of keys and refresh the cached permissions
decide whether a non-voting replica has caught up enough to become a full member
drop outgoing traffic to members that were removed and warn when heartbeats go out late
set up the pipeline, streams and message pumps for talking to another cluster member
turn a snapshot file into a fresh data directory a brand new member can boot from
merge watchers reading from the same point into one shared connection so fewer are opened upstream
refuse a transaction whose puts and deletes touch overlapping key ranges, nested branches included
try a failed call again and fetch a new auth token when the old one was rejected
periodically tell the server the leases this client holds are still in use
pick the storage size limit, falling back to a default and warning when it is too large
